name: Flutamide
summary: A prostate-cancer antiandrogen sometimes used off-label for female hirsutism and hair loss; liver toxicity makes it a last-line choice.
lead: Flutamide is a nonsteroidal antiandrogen that blocks the androgen receptor. It was the first drug of its type approved in the US, in 1989, for prostate cancer, and its labelled use is in combination with an LHRH agonist for locally confined and metastatic prostate carcinoma . Its label carries a boxed warning for liver injury and says it is for use only in men .
claims: Topical flutamide is a stronger anti-hair-loss option than topical spironolactone.
Oral flutamide is a hair-loss option but carries more side effects than other antiandrogens.

name: Bicalutamide
summary: A prostate-cancer antiandrogen used off-label for women's hair loss; supported by retrospective data only and with a liver-injury warning.
lead: Bicalutamide (brand name Casodex) is a nonsteroidal androgen-receptor antagonist. Its US label indicates the 50 mg dose in combination with an LHRH analogue for stage D2 metastatic prostate cancer, and states that 150 mg daily is not approved alone or with other treatments in the US .
claims: Bicalutamide might upregulate androgen receptors and help recover from post-isotretinoin or post-finasteride problems.
Oral antiandrogens like bicalutamide cause more side effects than topical options.
Low-dose bicalutamide treats female pattern hair loss.

name: Cyproterone acetate
summary: A progestin-antiandrogen used in women for hirsutism, acne and hair loss; effective in the clinic but limited by meningioma and liver risks.
lead: Cyproterone acetate (CPA) is a synthetic steroidal antiandrogen and progestin. It blocks androgen receptors and, through its progestogenic action, suppresses gonadotropin release and so lowers testosterone production in men and estradiol in women . It is used for palliation in advanced prostate cancer, for hirsutism and severe acne in women (often with ethinylestradiol), and to reduce sexual drive in men with paraphilias .

name: Latanoprost
summary: A glaucoma eye drop whose lash-lengthening and eye-darkening side effects get it mentioned in appearance circles; no cosmetic trials exist.
lead: Latanoprost is a synthetic prostaglandin F2-alpha analogue applied as an ophthalmic solution to lower raised intraocular pressure (IOP) in open-angle glaucoma and ocular hypertension. The US label describes its main action as increasing uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humour. It is a prescription medicine, and its approved use is medical rather than cosmetic.
claims: Prostaglandin drops such as latanoprost can make eyes darker
Latanoprost lengthens and thickens eyelashes

name: Onion juice
summary: A folk scalp remedy with one small alopecia areata trial behind it and reviews calling the evidence limited.
lead: Onion juice is the liquid pressed from the bulb of the common onion (Allium cepa), applied to the scalp as a folk remedy for hair loss and to encourage hair growth. It is discussed in reviews of social-media hair-loss advice alongside rosemary oil, rice water and garlic gel.
claims: Applying onion juice to the scalp regrows hair
Onion juice can replace conventional hair-loss treatments such as minoxidil or finasteride

name: Rosemary oil
summary: The natural minoxidil alternative: one small 2015 trial matched 2% minoxidil, but reviews call the evidence thin and a Canadian consensus did not recommend it.
lead: Rosemary oil is the essential oil steam-distilled from the leaves of the rosemary plant (Salvia rosmarinus, formerly Rosmarinus officinalis), long used in traditional medicine and cooking. In appearance communities it is applied to the scalp, and sometimes to eyebrows and lashes, as a natural hair-growth treatment and is frequently described as an alternative to minoxidil.
claims: Rosemary oil works about as well as minoxidil
Rosemary oil regulates hundreds of genes, possibly acting as an HDAC inhibitor
Castor oil plus rosemary oil thickens eyebrows and lashes
Ingesting rosemary lowers testosterone

name: Anastrozole
summary: A breast-cancer aromatase inhibitor that teen heightmaxxers and TRT users discuss for oestrogen control; no trials show a height gain in healthy people.
lead: Anastrozole, sold as Arimidex among other names, is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor taken by mouth. Its approved uses are in postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, where it lowers oestrogen by blocking the aromatase enzyme. It is a prescription medicine.
claims: Anastrozole delays growth-plate closure and increases adult height
Taken alone, anastrozole crashes oestrogen and bone mass
Anastrozole is better than exemestane for heightmaxxing because it has fewer androgenic effects
Long-term use causes lethargy and mental slowness

name: Letrozole
summary: A potent breast-cancer and fertility aromatase inhibitor that heightmaxxers eye for delaying growth plates; no trials in healthy teens, and forums warn of crashed oestrogen.
lead: Letrozole is a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor taken by mouth. The US label lists adjuvant and extended adjuvant treatment of hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer in postmenopausal women, and first- and second-line treatment of advanced disease. It is also widely used in fertility medicine for ovulation induction.
claims: Letrozole delays growth plate closure and adds height
Letrozole is more effective but riskier than exemestane
Crashing oestrogen is beneficial for gains or leanness

name: Exemestane
summary: A steroidal breast-cancer aromatase inhibitor teen heightmaxxers favour as the 'milder' option; no trials in healthy adolescents.
lead: Exemestane, sold as Aromasin, is an oral steroidal aromatase inhibitor that irreversibly inactivates the aromatase enzyme. The US label indicates it for adjuvant treatment of oestrogen-receptor-positive early breast cancer in postmenopausal women after two to three years of tamoxifen, and for advanced breast cancer progressing after tamoxifen. It is a prescription medicine.
claims: Exemestane keeps growth plates open and adds height
Exemestane is androgenic and therefore beneficial
Exemestane can permanently suppress oestrogen or cause hair loss

name: Tamoxifen
summary: A breast-cancer SERM that bodybuilders and TRT users take for gynecomastia; label carries a boxed warning and nothing tests it for looks.
lead: Tamoxifen, sold under the brand name Nolvadex among others, is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) taken by mouth. It acts as an oestrogen antagonist in breast tissue and as an agonist in some other tissues. The US label (for the oral solution Soltamox) lists treatment of metastatic breast cancer, adjuvant treatment of early-stage ER-positive breast cancer, reduction of risk after DCIS surgery, and risk reduction in high-risk women.
claims: Tamoxifen treats or reverses gynecomastia
Tamoxifen helps muscle gain by blocking oestrogen
SERMs like Nolvadex affect growth-plate closure

name: Clomiphene
summary: A fertility SERM that men use off-label to lift their own testosterone; some evidence in hypogonadal men, none for looks.
lead: Clomiphene citrate (Clomid) is a selective estrogen receptor modulator taken by mouth. The US label indicates it for ovulatory dysfunction in women desiring pregnancy, particularly polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). In men it is used off-label for hypogonadism, where it aims to raise the body's own testosterone and preserve sperm production, in contrast to exogenous testosterone.
claims: Clomid raises natural testosterone without injections
Enclomiphene raises testosterone more than clomiphene with fewer side effects
Clomiphene helps recovery after a steroid cycle

name: Enclomiphene
summary: The trans-isomer of clomiphene, studied for raising testosterone in men with secondary hypogonadism; forum use for appearance or height is largely untested.
lead: Enclomiphene (also called trans-clomiphene; the citrate salt was developed under the name Androxal) is a non-steroidal selective estrogen receptor modulator that behaves mainly as an estrogen receptor antagonist. It is the trans-stereoisomer of clomiphene citrate, a drug widely prescribed for decades for ovulatory dysfunction in women .
claims: Enclomiphene can raise testosterone into a high percentile range.
Enclomiphene can help height or bone growth.
It is a safer alternative to testosterone because it preserves fertility and testicle size.
Enclomiphene is useful in post-cycle therapy or after stopping TRT.

name: Nicotine
summary: The stimulant and addictive alkaloid in tobacco and pouches, used by some in appearance communities as an appetite suppressant; no trials test it for leanness, and its documented harms are well established.
lead: Nicotine is a plant alkaloid found chiefly in the tobacco plant and is the principal addictive component of tobacco products. It acts on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in the nervous system and increases release of dopamine and other neurotransmitters . It was isolated in 1828 according to one encyclopedic summary .
claims: Nicotine suppresses appetite and speeds up fat loss.
Nicotine improves focus and cognition.
Nicotine raises testosterone or blocks its conversion to estrogen.
Nicotine pouches harm looks (hair, skin, teeth, sleep).

name: Benzoyl peroxide
summary: The over-the-counter acne staple with a strong guideline recommendation and decades of trials; the main trade-off is dryness and irritation.
lead: Benzoyl peroxide (BPO) is an organic peroxide used topically for acne vulgaris and sold over the counter in washes, creams, gels and leave-on products, as well as in prescription combination products . It acts as an antibacterial and keratolytic agent .
claims: Benzoyl peroxide washes reduce body odor.
Benzoyl peroxide clears acne.
Higher strength (10%) works faster.
Benzoyl peroxide dries and irritates the skin.

name: Snail mucin
summary: The popular Korean-skincare ingredient made from snail secretion; reviews call it promising for hydration and scars but say large clinical trials are lacking.
lead: Snail mucin, or snail secretion filtrate (SSF), is a mucus secretion of snails used as a cosmetic ingredient, particularly in Korean skincare . It has been described as a mixture containing allantoin, glycolic acid, proteins, glycosaminoglycans, enzymes, peptides and trace minerals .

name: Centella asiatica
summary: Gotu kola, the 'cica' plant behind many calming Korean skincare products; trials on wound and scar healing exist, but evidence for anti-aging or looks is small and mixed in quality.
lead: Centella asiatica (gotu kola, Indian pennywort) is a herbaceous plant of the Apiaceae family used for centuries in Ayurvedic and traditional Chinese medicine . Its principal active compounds are pentacyclic triterpenes: asiaticoside, madecassoside, asiatic acid and madecassic acid .

name: Bakuchiol
summary: A plant-derived 'retinol alternative' for wrinkles and pigmentation, with a handful of small trials suggesting retinol-like results and less irritation.
lead: Bakuchiol is a meroterpene phenol obtained mainly from the seeds of Psoralea corylifolia, a plant used in traditional Indian and Chinese medicine for conditions such as psoriasis and leprosy . It has become a cosmetic ingredient promoted as a 'retinol alternative' for photoaging, wrinkles, hyperpigmentation and acne .

name: Mandelic acid
summary: A larger, slower-penetrating alpha-hydroxy acid used in gentle peels and serums for acne and dark spots; direct clinical evidence is thin.
lead: Mandelic acid (2-hydroxy-2-phenylacetic acid) is a chiral alpha-hydroxy acid with the formula C8H8O3 . In cosmetics and dermatology it is used as a chemical exfoliant for acne, hyperpigmentation and photoaging .

name: Tea tree oil
summary: Australian essential oil with proven lab antimicrobial activity and small acne and eyelid-mite trials; widely used topically, with contact allergy and toxicity if swallowed.
lead: Tea tree oil is an essential oil produced by steam distillation of Melaleuca alternifolia leaves, a plant native to eastern Australia, with terpinen-4-ol as its primary active component . A 2006 review describes it as used for almost 100 years in Australia and now sold worldwide as neat oil and as an ingredient in many products, chiefly for its antiseptic and anti-inflammatory properties .
claims: Tea tree oil helps prevent breakouts after shaving.
Tea tree oil lowers testosterone.
Tea tree oil reduces body odor and acne.

name: Squalane
summary: Shelf-stable, lightweight moisturising oil made from squalene; widely used in skincare, with little trial data of its own.
lead: Squalane is a saturated hydrocarbon (C30H62) made by hydrogenating squalene, a lipid found in human sebum, shark liver oil, olives and some other plant sources. It is a colourless, odourless, lightweight oil used mainly as an emollient and skin-conditioning ingredient in moisturisers, serums and hair products.

name: Sulfur (topical)
summary: Old-school OTC sulfur for acne and rosacea: long in use, with decent rosacea trial support and thinner acne data.
lead: Topical sulfur is one of the oldest dermatological treatments, used in lotions, creams, soaps, masks and spot treatments for acne, seborrhoeic dermatitis, rosacea and scabies. It is sold over the counter in the United States in products labelled for acne.

name: Topical finasteride
summary: Scalp-applied finasteride aimed at cutting systemic DHT and side effects; trial data are encouraging but smaller than for the oral drug.
lead: Topical finasteride is finasteride, a type II 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor, formulated for application to the scalp rather than taken as a daily tablet. It is used off-label or as a compounded or newer branded preparation for androgenetic alopecia (male and female pattern hair loss), with the stated aim of reducing the drug's systemic exposure and thereby its side effects.
claims: Topical finasteride only lowers scalp DHT, so it avoids oral side effects
Topical finasteride lowers serum DHT about as much as the oral drug
A slowly escalating ultra-low topical dose lets the body adjust and lowers side-effect risk
Topical dutasteride or other antiandrogens avoid the serum DHT effect of topical finasteride

name: Fluridil
summary: Obscure topical antiandrogen (Eucapil) for hair loss, backed by a single small 2002 trial.
lead: Fluridil (marketed in Europe under the name Eucapil) is a topical antiandrogen developed for androgenetic alopecia. Its authors describe it as a novel agent that suppresses the human androgen receptor locally in the scalp, is highly hydrophobic and breaks down by hydrolysis, and is not absorbed systemically.
claims: Fluridil is a topical antiandrogen option for hair loss that avoids systemic effects

name: Caffeine shampoo
summary: Marketed anti-hair-loss shampoo (Alpecin and others); one women's trial exists, with little else behind it.
lead: Caffeine shampoo refers to cosmetic shampoos containing caffeine, marketed for people with thinning hair; the best-known brand is Alpecin. The idea is that caffeine applied to the scalp may counter the effects of androgens on hair follicles.

name: Tongkat ali
summary: Southeast Asian root extract sold as a 'natural test booster'; small trials lean positive, but broader reviews are sceptical.
lead: Tongkat ali (Eurycoma longifolia, also called longjack or Malaysian ginseng) is a Southeast Asian shrub whose root is used in traditional medicine as an aphrodisiac and for fever, and is now sold worldwide as a dietary supplement marketed as a natural testosterone booster. The roots contain quassinoids and alkaloids such as eurycomanone.
claims: Tongkat ali raises testosterone naturally
Tongkat ali improves libido and erectile function
Tongkat ali lowers cortisol and improves body composition
Natural testosterone from tongkat ali rivals or beats injected testosterone

name: Fadogia agrestis
summary: Podcast-famous African stem extract sold as a testosterone booster; supported only by rat studies, with toxicity questions unanswered in humans.
lead: Fadogia agrestis (now often classified as Vangueria agrestis) is a plant of the coffee family, Rubiaceae, native to tropical Africa. Its stem has been used in traditional African medicine as an aphrodisiac and for pain and inflammation, and extracts are sold as dietary supplements marketed for testosterone and libido.
claims: Fadogia agrestis raises testosterone in men
Fadogia can help restore testicular function or recovery after steroid or hormone use
Fadogia is safe at supplement doses
Stacking Fadogia with tongkat ali is synergistic

name: Shilajit
summary: Himalayan mineral resin sold for testosterone and vitality; one small trial supports a testosterone rise, and quality control is the open question.
lead: Shilajit (also mumijo, moumiyo or mummiyo) is a sticky, dark, tar-like substance that seeps from rock layers in high mountain ranges such as the Himalayas, long used in Ayurvedic and other traditional medicine as a rejuvenator (rasayana) and adaptogen. It consists mainly of humic substances (a review puts them at more than 80 percent of its weight) together with minerals and plant and microbial metabolites.
claims: Shilajit raises testosterone
Shilajit boosts alertness, energy and recovery
Higher-altitude 'gold grade' shilajit is purer and more potent
Shilajit helps bones, collagen, brain and ageing

name: Cistanche
summary: A Chinese tonic herb that bodybuilding forums list as a test and DHT booster; human trials on those claims are essentially absent.
lead: Cistanche is a genus of parasitic desert plants whose fleshy stems, chiefly from Cistanche deserticola and Cistanche tubulosa, are used as a tonic in traditional Chinese medicine under the name Rou Cong Rong, sometimes called "desert ginseng" . Traditional uses include treating kidney deficiency, impotence, female infertility and constipation in older people .
claims: Cistanche tubulosa extract is a "DHT boost" or test booster
Cistanche helps libido and erectile function after a cycle
Cistanche improves muscle strength and recovery
Herbal blends including Cistanche may harm organs

name: Kisspeptin
summary: A hypothalamic peptide that triggers LH release; forums pitch kisspeptin-10 as an hCG alternative, but no trial tests that use.
lead: Kisspeptins are a family of neuropeptides encoded by the KISS1 gene. They act on the receptor KISS1R (GPR54) on gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neurons in the hypothalamus, which makes them a key upstream signal for luteinizing hormone (LH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and, in men, testosterone . The shortest fully active fragment, kisspeptin-10, and the longer kisspeptin-54 have both been given to people in research settings .
claims: Kisspeptin-10 can replace hCG to keep the testes active on TRT
Kisspeptin does not desensitise the way gonadorelin does
Kisspeptin restores libido
Kisspeptin helps post-cycle recovery of natural production

name: Gonadorelin
summary: Synthetic GnRH that TRT forums use as an hCG substitute; established for fertility medicine, untested for that use.
lead: Gonadorelin is the synthetic form of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), the hypothalamic decapeptide that prompts the pituitary to release luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) . In medicine it has been used to test pituitary responsiveness and, delivered in pulses, to induce ovulation in women with hypothalamic amenorrhea .
claims: Gonadorelin can replace hCG to prevent testicular atrophy on TRT
Gonadorelin's short half-life makes it ineffective against atrophy
Gonadorelin avoids hCG side effects such as gynecomastia or poor tolerance
